items.title: Elements and interfaces identified
items.pass_criterion: Every system element (hardware, software, other technology, or external system) and every interface has a unique ID and a defined responsibility.
items.typical_defect: Element or interface without ID; two elements with the same ID.

items.title: System requirement allocation complete
items.pass_criterion: Every system requirement is allocated to at least one system element, and the architecture references no unknown requirement ID.
items.typical_defect: System requirement allocated to no element.

items.title: Interfaces specified
items.pass_criterion: Internal and external interfaces, including the hardware-software interface (HSI), define signals or data, protocols, ranges, timing and error behaviour.
items.typical_defect: Interface named but without data ranges, timing or error behaviour.

items.title: Hardware/software allocation justified
items.pass_criterion: The allocation of functions to hardware and software elements is justified, and the requirements derived for each element are identified.
items.typical_defect: Function placed in software with no rationale; derived element requirements missing.

items.title: Dynamic behaviour specified
items.pass_criterion: Operating modes, state transitions, start-up/shutdown and timing interactions between elements are specified.
items.typical_defect: No mode or state model; start-up ordering between elements undefined.

items.title: Architecture analysed
items.pass_criterion: Design decisions and alternatives are recorded with criteria; feasibility, timing and resource budgets across elements are analysed.
items.typical_defect: Architecture chosen with no recorded criteria or budget analysis.

items.title: Safety mechanisms allocated
items.pass_criterion: Where integrity requirements apply, safety mechanisms, fault detection and reaction, safe states, integrity levels and independence or freedom from interference are allocated to elements.
items.typical_defect: Safe-state requirement with no mechanism or element realising it.

items.title: Consistency and bidirectional traceability
items.pass_criterion: Requirements and architecture elements are traced in both directions, and the linked content is consistent in meaning.
items.typical_defect: Element linked to a requirement it does not realise; contradicting interface definitions.

items.title: Verification readiness
items.pass_criterion: Each element and interface can be verified during system integration; integration-relevant properties and observation points are identified.
items.typical_defect: Interface property with no way to observe or stimulate it during integration.

items.title: Agreed and baselined
items.pass_criterion: The agreed architecture is baselined with version identity; open issues and affected parties are recorded.
items.typical_defect: Architecture used downstream with no version or recorded open issues.
